17 # Affine maps
18 
19 This file defines affine maps.
20 
21 ## Main definitions
22 
23 * `AffineMap` is the type of affine maps between two affine spaces with the same ring `k`.  Various
24   basic examples of affine maps are defined, including `const`, `id`, `lineMap` and `homothety`.
25 
26 ## Notation
27 
28 * `P1 →ᵃ[k] P2` is a notation for `AffineMap k P1 P2`;
29 * `AffineSpace V P`: a localized notation for `AddTorsor V P` defined in
30   `LinearAlgebra.AffineSpace.Basic`.
31 
32 ## Implementation notes
33 
34 `outParam` is used in the definition of `[AddTorsor V P]` to make `V` an implicit argument
35 (deduced from `P`) in most cases. As for modules, `k` is an explicit argument rather than implied by
36 `P` or `V`.
37 
38 This file only provides purely algebraic definitions and results. Those depending on analysis or
39 topology are defined elsewhere; see `Analysis.Normed.Affine.AddTorsor` and
40 `Topology.Algebra.Affine`.
41 
42 ## References
43 
44 * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affine_space
45 * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_homogeneous_space
46 -/

52 /-- An `AffineMap k P1 P2` (notation: `P1 →ᵃ[k] P2`) is a map from `P1` to `P2` that
53 induces a corresponding linear map from `V1` to `V2`. -/
54 structure AffineMap (k : Type*) {V1 : Type*} (P1 : Type*) {V2 : Type*} (P2 : Type*) [Ring k]
55   [AddCommGroup V1] [Module k V1] [AffineSpace V1 P1] [AddCommGroup V2] [Module k V2]
56   [AffineSpace V2 P2] where
57   /-- The underlying function between the affine spaces `P1` and `P2`. -/
58   toFun : P1 → P2
59   /-- The linear map between the corresponding vector spaces `V1` and `V2`.
60   This represents how the affine map acts on differences of points. -/
61   linear : V1 →ₗ[k] V2
62   map_vadd' : ∀ (p : P1) (v : V1), toFun (v +ᵥ p) = linear v +ᵥ toFun p
63 
64 /-- An `AffineMap k P1 P2` (notation: `P1 →ᵃ[k] P2`) is a map from `P1` to `P2` that
65 induces a corresponding linear map from `V1` to `V2`. -/
66 notation:25 P1 " →ᵃ[" k:25 "] " P2:0 => AffineMap k P1 P2
67 
68 instance AffineMap.instFunLike (k : Type*) {V1 : Type*} (P1 : Type*) {V2 : Type*} (P2 : Type*)
69     [Ring k] [AddCommGroup V1] [Module k V1] [AffineSpace V1 P1] [AddCommGroup V2] [Module k V2]
70     [AffineSpace V2 P2] : FunLike (P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) P1 P2 where
71   coe := AffineMap.toFun
72   coe_injective' := fun ⟨f, f_linear, f_add⟩ ⟨g, g_linear, g_add⟩ => fun (h : f = g) => by
73     obtain ⟨p⟩ := (AddTorsor.nonempty : Nonempty P1)
74     congr with v
75     apply vadd_right_cancel (f p)
76     rw [← f_add, h, ← g_add]

83 /-- Reinterpret a linear map as an affine map. -/
84 def toAffineMap : V₁ →ᵃ[k] V₂ where
85   toFun := f
86   linear := f
87   map_vadd' p v := f.map_add v p

95   rfl

106 /-- Constructing an affine map and coercing back to a function
107 produces the same map. -/
108 @[simp]
109 theorem coe_mk (f : P1 → P2) (linear add) : ((mk f linear add : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) : P1 → P2) = f :=
110   rfl
111 
112 /-- `toFun` is the same as the result of coercing to a function. -/
113 @[simp]
114 theorem toFun_eq_coe (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) : f.toFun = ⇑f :=
115   rfl
116 
117 /-- An affine map on the result of adding a vector to a point produces
118 the same result as the linear map applied to that vector, added to the
119 affine map applied to that point. -/
120 @[simp]
121 theorem map_vadd (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) (p : P1) (v : V1) : f (v +ᵥ p) = f.linear v +ᵥ f p :=
122   f.map_vadd' p v
123 
124 /-- The linear map on the result of subtracting two points is the
125 result of subtracting the result of the affine map on those two
126 points. -/
127 @[simp]
128 theorem linearMap_vsub (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) (p1 p2 : P1) : f.linear (p1 -ᵥ p2) = f p1 -ᵥ f p2 := by
129   conv_rhs => rw [← vsub_vadd p1 p2, map_vadd, vadd_vsub]
130 
131 /-- Two affine maps are equal if they coerce to the same function. -/
132 @[ext]
133 theorem ext {f g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2} (h : ∀ p, f p = g p) : f = g :=
134   DFunLike.ext _ _ h
135 
136 theorem coeFn_injective : @Function.Injective (P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) (P1 → P2) (⇑) :=
137   DFunLike.coe_injective
138 
139 protected theorem congr_arg (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) {x y : P1} (h : x = y) : f x = f y :=
140   congr_arg _ h
141 
142 protected theorem congr_fun {f g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2} (h : f = g) (x : P1) : f x = g x :=
143   h ▸ rfl
144 
145 /-- Two affine maps are equal if they have equal linear maps and are equal at some point. -/
146 theorem ext_linear {f g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2} (h₁ : f.linear = g.linear) {p : P1} (h₂ : f p = g p) :
147     f = g := by
148   ext q
149   have hgl : g.linear (q -ᵥ p) = toFun g ((q -ᵥ p) +ᵥ q) -ᵥ toFun g q := by simp
150   have := f.map_vadd' q (q -ᵥ p)
151   rw [h₁, hgl, toFun_eq_coe, map_vadd, linearMap_vsub, h₂] at this
152   simpa
153 
154 /-- Two affine maps are equal if they have equal linear maps and are equal at some point. -/
155 theorem ext_linear_iff {f g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2} : f = g ↔ (f.linear = g.linear) ∧ (∃ p, f p = g p) :=
156   ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨congrArg _ h, by inhabit P1; exact default, by rw [h]⟩,
157   fun h ↦ Exists.casesOn h.2 fun _ hp ↦ ext_linear h.1 hp⟩

182 theorem linear_eq_zero_iff_exists_const (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) :
183     f.linear = 0 ↔ ∃ q, f = const k P1 q := by
184   refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h => ?_⟩
185   · use f (Classical.arbitrary P1)
186     ext
187     rw [coe_const, Function.const_apply, ← @vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq V2, ← f.linearMap_vsub, h,
188       LinearMap.zero_apply]
189   · rcases h with ⟨q, rfl⟩
190     exact const_linear k P1 q

195 /-- Construct an affine map by verifying the relation between the map and its linear part at one
196 base point. Namely, this function takes a map `f : P₁ → P₂`, a linear map `f' : V₁ →ₗ[k] V₂`, and
197 a point `p` such that for any other point `p'` we have `f p' = f' (p' -ᵥ p) +ᵥ f p`. -/
198 def mk' (f : P1 → P2) (f' : V1 →ₗ[k] V2) (p : P1) (h : ∀ p' : P1, f p' = f' (p' -ᵥ p) +ᵥ f p) :
199     P1 →ᵃ[k] P2 where
200   toFun := f
201   linear := f'
202   map_vadd' p' v := by rw [h, h p', vadd_vsub_assoc, f'.map_add, vadd_vadd]
203 
204 @[simp]
205 theorem coe_mk' (f : P1 → P2) (f' : V1 →ₗ[k] V2) (p h) : ⇑(mk' f f' p h) = f :=
206   rfl
207 
208 @[simp]
209 theorem mk'_linear (f : P1 → P2) (f' : V1 →ₗ[k] V2) (p h) : (mk' f f' p h).linear = f' :=
210   rfl

278 /-- The set of affine maps to a vector space is an additive commutative group. -/
279 instance : AddCommGroup (P1 →ᵃ[k] V2) :=
280   coeFn_injective.addCommGroup _ coe_zero coe_add coe_neg coe_sub (fun _ _ => coe_smul _ _)
281     fun _ _ => coe_smul _ _
282 
283 /-- The space of affine maps from `P1` to `P2` is an affine space over the space of affine maps
284 from `P1` to the vector space `V2` corresponding to `P2`. -/
285 instance : AffineSpace (P1 →ᵃ[k] V2) (P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) where
286   vadd f g :=
287     ⟨fun p => f p +ᵥ g p, f.linear + g.linear,
288       fun p v => by simp [vadd_vadd, add_right_comm]⟩
289   zero_vadd f := ext fun p => zero_vadd _ (f p)
290   add_vadd f₁ f₂ f₃ := ext fun p => add_vadd (f₁ p) (f₂ p) (f₃ p)
291   vsub f g :=
292     ⟨fun p => f p -ᵥ g p, f.linear - g.linear, fun p v => by
293       simp [vsub_vadd_eq_vsub_sub, vadd_vsub_assoc, sub_add_eq_add_sub]⟩
294   vsub_vadd' f g := ext fun p => vsub_vadd (f p) (g p)
295   vadd_vsub' f g := ext fun p => vadd_vsub (f p) (g p)
296

368 /-- Composition of affine maps. -/
369 @[simps linear]
370 def comp (f : P2 →ᵃ[k] P3) (g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) : P1 →ᵃ[k] P3 where
371   toFun := f ∘ g
372   linear := f.linear.comp g.linear
373   map_vadd' := by
374     intro p v
375     rw [Function.comp_apply, g.map_vadd, f.map_vadd]
376     rfl
377 
378 /-- Composition of affine maps acts as applying the two functions. -/
379 @[simp]
380 theorem coe_comp (f : P2 →ᵃ[k] P3) (g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) : ⇑(f.comp g) = f ∘ g :=
381   rfl
382 
383 /-- Composition of affine maps acts as applying the two functions. -/
384 theorem comp_apply (f : P2 →ᵃ[k] P3) (g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) (p : P1) : f.comp g p = f (g p) :=
385   rfl
386 
387 @[simp]
388 theorem comp_id (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) : f.comp (id k P1) = f :=
389   ext fun _ => rfl
390 
391 @[simp]
392 theorem id_comp (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) : (id k P2).comp f = f :=

395 theorem comp_assoc (f₃₄ : P3 →ᵃ[k] P4) (f₂₃ : P2 →ᵃ[k] P3) (f₁₂ : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) :
396     (f₃₄.comp f₂₃).comp f₁₂ = f₃₄.comp (f₂₃.comp f₁₂) :=
397   rfl

422 theorem linear_injective_iff (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) :
423     Function.Injective f.linear ↔ Function.Injective f := by
424   obtain ⟨p⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty P1)
425   have h : ⇑f.linear = (Equiv.vaddConst (f p)).symm ∘ f ∘ Equiv.vaddConst p := by
426     ext v
427     simp [f.map_vadd]
428   rw [h, Equiv.comp_injective, Equiv.injective_comp]
429 
430 @[simp]
431 theorem linear_surjective_iff (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) :
432     Function.Surjective f.linear ↔ Function.Surjective f := by
433   obtain ⟨p⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty P1)
434   have h : ⇑f.linear = (Equiv.vaddConst (f p)).symm ∘ f ∘ Equiv.vaddConst p := by
435     ext v
436     simp [f.map_vadd]
437   rw [h, Equiv.comp_surjective, Equiv.surjective_comp]

441     Function.Bijective f.linear ↔ Function.Bijective f :=

445     f '' s -ᵥ f '' t = f.linear '' (s -ᵥ t) := by
446   ext v

448     exists_exists_and_eq_and, ← f.linearMap_vsub]
449   grind

479 /-! ### Definition of `AffineMap.lineMap` and lemmas about it -/
480 
481 /-- The affine map from `k` to `P1` sending `0` to `p₀` and `1` to `p₁`. -/
482 def lineMap (p₀ p₁ : P1) : k →ᵃ[k] P1 :=
483   ((LinearMap.id : k →ₗ[k] k).smulRight (p₁ -ᵥ p₀)).toAffineMap +ᵥ const k k p₀
484 
485 theorem coe_lineMap (p₀ p₁ : P1) : (lineMap p₀ p₁ : k → P1) = fun c => c • (p₁ -ᵥ p₀) +ᵥ p₀ :=
486   rfl
487 
488 theorem lineMap_apply (p₀ p₁ : P1) (c : k) : lineMap p₀ p₁ c = c • (p₁ -ᵥ p₀) +ᵥ p₀ :=
489   rfl
490 
491 theorem lineMap_apply_module' (p₀ p₁ : V1) (c : k) : lineMap p₀ p₁ c = c • (p₁ - p₀) + p₀ :=
492   rfl
493 
494 theorem lineMap_apply_module (p₀ p₁ : V1) (c : k) : lineMap p₀ p₁ c = (1 - c) • p₀ + c • p₁ := by
495   simp [lineMap_apply_module', smul_sub, sub_smul]; abel
496 
497 theorem lineMap_apply_ring' (a b c : k) : lineMap a b c = c * (b - a) + a :=
498   rfl
499 
500 theorem lineMap_apply_ring (a b c : k) : lineMap a b c = (1 - c) * a + c * b :=
501   lineMap_apply_module a b c
502 
503 theorem lineMap_vadd_apply (p : P1) (v : V1) (c : k) : lineMap p (v +ᵥ p) c = c • v +ᵥ p := by
504   rw [lineMap_apply, vadd_vsub]
505 
506 @[simp]
507 theorem lineMap_linear (p₀ p₁ : P1) :
508     (lineMap p₀ p₁ : k →ᵃ[k] P1).linear = LinearMap.id.smulRight (p₁ -ᵥ p₀) :=
509   add_zero _
510 
511 theorem lineMap_same_apply (p : P1) (c : k) : lineMap p p c = p := by
512   simp [lineMap_apply]
513 
514 @[simp]
515 theorem lineMap_same (p : P1) : lineMap p p = const k k p :=
516   ext <| lineMap_same_apply p
517 
518 @[simp]
519 theorem lineMap_apply_zero (p₀ p₁ : P1) : lineMap p₀ p₁ (0 : k) = p₀ := by
520   simp [lineMap_apply]
521 
522 @[simp]
523 theorem lineMap_apply_one (p₀ p₁ : P1) : lineMap p₀ p₁ (1 : k) = p₁ := by
524   simp [lineMap_apply]
525 
526 @[simp]
527 theorem lineMap_eq_lineMap_iff [IsDomain k] [IsTorsionFree k V1] {p₀ p₁ : P1} {c₁ c₂ : k} :
528     lineMap p₀ p₁ c₁ = lineMap p₀ p₁ c₂ ↔ p₀ = p₁ ∨ c₁ = c₂ := by
529   rw [lineMap_apply, lineMap_apply, ← @vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq V1, vadd_vsub_vadd_cancel_right, ←
530     sub_smul, smul_eq_zero, sub_eq_zero, vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq, or_comm, eq_comm]
531 
532 @[simp]
533 theorem lineMap_eq_left_iff [IsDomain k] [IsTorsionFree k V1] {p₀ p₁ : P1} {c : k} :
534     lineMap p₀ p₁ c = p₀ ↔ p₀ = p₁ ∨ c = 0 := by
535   rw [← @lineMap_eq_lineMap_iff k V1, lineMap_apply_zero]
536 
537 @[simp]
538 theorem lineMap_eq_right_iff [IsDomain k] [IsTorsionFree k V1] {p₀ p₁ : P1} {c : k} :
539     lineMap p₀ p₁ c = p₁ ↔ p₀ = p₁ ∨ c = 1 := by
540   rw [← @lineMap_eq_lineMap_iff k V1, lineMap_apply_one]
541 
542 variable (k) in
543 theorem lineMap_injective [IsDomain k] [IsTorsionFree k V1] {p₀ p₁ : P1} (h : p₀ ≠ p₁) :
544     Function.Injective (lineMap p₀ p₁ : k → P1) := fun _c₁ _c₂ hc =>
545   (lineMap_eq_lineMap_iff.mp hc).resolve_left h
546 
547 @[simp]
548 theorem apply_lineMap (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) (p₀ p₁ : P1) (c : k) :
549     f (lineMap p₀ p₁ c) = lineMap (f p₀) (f p₁) c := by
550   simp [lineMap_apply]
551 
552 @[simp]
553 theorem comp_lineMap (f : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) (p₀ p₁ : P1) :
554     f.comp (lineMap p₀ p₁) = lineMap (f p₀) (f p₁) :=
555   ext <| f.apply_lineMap p₀ p₁
556 
557 @[simp]
558 theorem fst_lineMap (p₀ p₁ : P1 × P2) (c : k) : (lineMap p₀ p₁ c).1 = lineMap p₀.1 p₁.1 c :=
559   fst.apply_lineMap p₀ p₁ c
560 
561 @[simp]
562 theorem snd_lineMap (p₀ p₁ : P1 × P2) (c : k) : (lineMap p₀ p₁ c).2 = lineMap p₀.2 p₁.2 c :=
563   snd.apply_lineMap p₀ p₁ c
564 
565 theorem lineMap_symm (p₀ p₁ : P1) :
566     lineMap p₀ p₁ = (lineMap p₁ p₀).comp (lineMap (1 : k) (0 : k)) := by
567   simp
568 
569 @[simp]
570 theorem lineMap_apply_one_sub (p₀ p₁ : P1) (c : k) : lineMap p₀ p₁ (1 - c) = lineMap p₁ p₀ c := by
571   rw [lineMap_symm p₀, comp_apply]
572   congr
573   simp [lineMap_apply]
574 
575 @[simp]
576 theorem lineMap_vsub_left (p₀ p₁ : P1) (c : k) : lineMap p₀ p₁ c -ᵥ p₀ = c • (p₁ -ᵥ p₀) :=
577   vadd_vsub _ _
578 
579 @[simp]
580 theorem left_vsub_lineMap (p₀ p₁ : P1) (c : k) : p₀ -ᵥ lineMap p₀ p₁ c = c • (p₀ -ᵥ p₁) := by
581   rw [← neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev, lineMap_vsub_left, ← smul_neg, neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev]
582 
583 @[simp]
584 theorem lineMap_vsub_right (p₀ p₁ : P1) (c : k) : lineMap p₀ p₁ c -ᵥ p₁ = (1 - c) • (p₀ -ᵥ p₁) := by
585   rw [← lineMap_apply_one_sub, lineMap_vsub_left]
586 
587 @[simp]
588 theorem right_vsub_lineMap (p₀ p₁ : P1) (c : k) : p₁ -ᵥ lineMap p₀ p₁ c = (1 - c) • (p₁ -ᵥ p₀) := by
589   rw [← lineMap_apply_one_sub, left_vsub_lineMap]
590 
591 theorem lineMap_vadd_lineMap (v₁ v₂ : V1) (p₁ p₂ : P1) (c : k) :
592     lineMap v₁ v₂ c +ᵥ lineMap p₁ p₂ c = lineMap (v₁ +ᵥ p₁) (v₂ +ᵥ p₂) c :=
593   ((fst : V1 × P1 →ᵃ[k] V1) +ᵥ (snd : V1 × P1 →ᵃ[k] P1)).apply_lineMap (v₁, p₁) (v₂, p₂) c
594 
595 theorem lineMap_vsub_lineMap (p₁ p₂ p₃ p₄ : P1) (c : k) :
596     lineMap p₁ p₂ c -ᵥ lineMap p₃ p₄ c = lineMap (p₁ -ᵥ p₃) (p₂ -ᵥ p₄) c :=
597   ((fst : P1 × P1 →ᵃ[k] P1) -ᵥ (snd : P1 × P1 →ᵃ[k] P1)).apply_lineMap (_, _) (_, _) c
598 
599 @[simp] lemma lineMap_lineMap_right (p₀ p₁ : P1) (c d : k) :
600     lineMap p₀ (lineMap p₀ p₁ c) d = lineMap p₀ p₁ (d * c) := by simp [lineMap_apply, mul_smul]
601 
602 @[simp] lemma lineMap_lineMap_left (p₀ p₁ : P1) (c d : k) :
603     lineMap (lineMap p₀ p₁ c) p₁ d = lineMap p₀ p₁ (1 - (1 - d) * (1 - c)) := by
604   simp_rw [lineMap_apply_one_sub, ← lineMap_apply_one_sub p₁, lineMap_lineMap_right]
605 
606 lemma lineMap_mono [LinearOrder k] [Preorder V1] [AddRightMono V1] [SMulPosMono k V1]
607     {p₀ p₁ : V1} (h : p₀ ≤ p₁) :
608     Monotone (lineMap (k := k) p₀ p₁) := by
609   intro x y hxy
610   suffices x • (p₁ - p₀) ≤ y • (p₁ - p₀) by simpa [lineMap]
611   gcongr
612   simpa
613 
614 lemma lineMap_anti [LinearOrder k] [Preorder V1] [AddLeftMono V1] [SMulPosMono k V1]
615     {p₀ p₁ : V1} (h : p₁ ≤ p₀) :
616     Antitone (lineMap (k := k) p₀ p₁) := by
617   intro x y hxy
618   suffices y • (p₁ - p₀) ≤ x • (p₁ - p₀) by simpa [lineMap]
619   rw [← neg_le_neg_iff, ← smul_neg, ← smul_neg]
620   gcongr
621   simpa
622 
623 /-- Decomposition of an affine map in the special case when the point space and vector space
624 are the same. -/
625 theorem decomp (f : V1 →ᵃ[k] V2) : (f : V1 → V2) = ⇑f.linear + fun _ => f 0 := by
626   ext x
627   calc
628     f x = f.linear x +ᵥ f 0 := by rw [← f.map_vadd, vadd_eq_add, add_zero]
629     _ = (f.linear + fun _ : V1 => f 0) x := rfl
630 
631 /-- Decomposition of an affine map in the special case when the point space and vector space
632 are the same. -/
633 theorem decomp' (f : V1 →ᵃ[k] V2) : (f.linear : V1 → V2) = ⇑f - fun _ => f 0 := by
634   rw [decomp]
635   simp only [map_zero, Pi.add_apply, add_sub_cancel_right, zero_add]
636 
637 theorem image_uIcc {k : Type*} [Field k] [LinearOrder k] [IsStrictOrderedRing k]
638     (f : k →ᵃ[k] k) (a b : k) :
639     f '' Set.uIcc a b = Set.uIcc (f a) (f b) := by
640   have : ⇑f = (fun x => x + f 0) ∘ fun x => x * (f 1 - f 0) := by
641     ext x
642     change f x = x • (f 1 -ᵥ f 0) +ᵥ f 0
643     rw [← f.linearMap_vsub, ← f.linear.map_smul, ← f.map_vadd]
644     simp only [vsub_eq_sub, add_zero, mul_one, vadd_eq_add, sub_zero, smul_eq_mul]
645   rw [this, Set.image_comp]
646   simp only [Set.image_add_const_uIcc, Set.image_mul_const_uIcc, Function.comp_apply]
647

649 
650 variable {ι : Type*} {V : ι → Type*} {P : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (V i)]
651   [∀ i, Module k (V i)] [∀ i, AddTorsor (V i) (P i)]
652 
653 /-- Evaluation at a point as an affine map. -/
654 def proj (i : ι) : (∀ i : ι, P i) →ᵃ[k] P i where
655   toFun f := f i
656   linear := @LinearMap.proj k ι _ V _ _ i
657   map_vadd' _ _ := rfl
658 
659 @[simp]
660 theorem proj_apply (i : ι) (f : ∀ i, P i) : @proj k _ ι V P _ _ _ i f = f i :=
661   rfl
662 
663 @[simp]
664 theorem proj_linear (i : ι) : (@proj k _ ι V P _ _ _ i).linear = @LinearMap.proj k ι _ V _ _ i :=
665   rfl
666 
667 theorem pi_lineMap_apply (f g : ∀ i, P i) (c : k) (i : ι) :
668     lineMap f g c i = lineMap (f i) (g i) c :=
669   (proj i : (∀ i, P i) →ᵃ[k] P i).apply_lineMap f g c
670 
671 end
672 
673 end AffineMap

678 
679 section Ring
680 
681 variable [Ring k] [AddCommGroup V1] [AffineSpace V1 P1] [AddCommGroup V2] [AffineSpace V2 P2]
682 variable [AddCommGroup V3] [AffineSpace V3 P3] [Module k V1] [Module k V2] [Module k V3]

684 section DistribMulAction
685 
686 variable [Monoid R] [DistribMulAction R V2] [SMulCommClass k R V2]
687 
688 /-- The space of affine maps to a module inherits an `R`-action from the action on its codomain. -/
689 instance distribMulAction : DistribMulAction R (P1 →ᵃ[k] V2) where
690   smul_add _ _ _ := ext fun _ => smul_add _ _ _
691   smul_zero _ := ext fun _ => smul_zero _
692 
693 end DistribMulAction
694 
695 section Module
696 
697 variable [Semiring R] [Module R V2] [SMulCommClass k R V2]
698 
699 /-- The space of affine maps taking values in an `R`-module is an `R`-module. -/
700 instance : Module R (P1 →ᵃ[k] V2) :=
701   { AffineMap.distribMulAction with
702     add_smul := fun _ _ _ => ext fun _ => add_smul _ _ _
703     zero_smul := fun _ => ext fun _ => zero_smul _ _ }
704 
705 variable (R)
706 
707 /-- The space of affine maps between two modules is linearly equivalent to the product of the
708 domain with the space of linear maps, by taking the value of the affine map at `(0 : V1)` and the
709 linear part.
710 
711 See note [bundled maps over different rings] -/
712 @[simps]
713 def toConstProdLinearMap : (V1 →ᵃ[k] V2) ≃ₗ[R] V2 × (V1 →ₗ[k] V2) where
714   toFun f := ⟨f 0, f.linear⟩
715   invFun p := p.2.toAffineMap + const k V1 p.1
716   left_inv f := by
717     ext
718     rw [f.decomp]
719     simp
720   right_inv := by
721     rintro ⟨v, f⟩
722     ext <;> simp [const_linear]
723   map_add' := by simp
724   map_smul' := by simp
725 
726 end Module
727 
728 /-- Interpolating between affine maps with `lineMap` commutes with evaluation. -/
729 @[simp]
730 lemma lineMap_apply' [SMulCommClass k k V2] (f g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) (c : k)
731     (p : P1) : lineMap f g c p = lineMap (f p) (g p) c := by
732   simp [AffineMap.lineMap_apply]

734 section Pi
735 
736 variable {ι : Type*} {φv φp : ι → Type*} [(i : ι) → AddCommGroup (φv i)]
737   [(i : ι) → Module k (φv i)] [(i : ι) → AffineSpace (φv i) (φp i)]
738 /-- `pi` construction for affine maps. From a family of affine maps it produces an affine
739 map into a family of affine spaces.
740 
741 This is the affine version of `LinearMap.pi`.
742 -/
743 @[simps linear]
744 def pi (f : (i : ι) → (P1 →ᵃ[k] φp i)) : P1 →ᵃ[k] ((i : ι) → φp i) where
745   toFun m a := f a m
746   linear := LinearMap.pi (fun a ↦ (f a).linear)
747   map_vadd' _ _ := funext fun _ ↦ map_vadd _ _ _
748 
749 --fp for when the image is a dependent AffineSpace φp i, fv for when the
750 --image is a Module φv i, f' for when the image isn't dependent.
751 variable (fp : (i : ι) → (P1 →ᵃ[k] φp i)) (fv : (i : ι) → (P1 →ᵃ[k] φv i))
752   (f' : ι → P1 →ᵃ[k] P2)
753 
754 @[simp]
755 theorem pi_apply (c : P1) (i : ι) : pi fp c i = fp i c :=
756   rfl
757 
758 theorem pi_comp (g : P3 →ᵃ[k] P1) : (pi fp).comp g = pi (fun i => (fp i).comp g) :=
759   rfl
760 
761 theorem pi_eq_zero : pi fv = 0 ↔ ∀ i, fv i = 0 := by
762   simp only [AffineMap.ext_iff, funext_iff, pi_apply]
763   exact forall_comm
764 
765 theorem pi_zero : pi (fun _ ↦ 0 : (i : ι) → P1 →ᵃ[k] φv i) = 0 := by
766   ext; rfl
767 
768 theorem proj_pi (i : ι) : (proj i).comp (pi fp) = fp i :=
769   ext fun _ => rfl
770 section Ext
771 
772 variable [Finite ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f g : ((i : ι) → φv i) →ᵃ[k] P2}
773 
774 /-- Two affine maps from a Pi-type of modules `(i : ι) → φv i` are equal if they are equal in their
775   operation on `Pi.single` and at zero. Analogous to `LinearMap.pi_ext`. See also `pi_ext_nonempty`,
776   which instead of agreement at zero requires `Nonempty ι`. -/
777 theorem pi_ext_zero (h : ∀ i x, f (Pi.single i x) = g (Pi.single i x)) (h₂ : f 0 = g 0) :
778     f = g := by
779   apply ext_linear
780   · apply LinearMap.pi_ext
781     intro i x
782     have s₁ := h i x
783     have s₂ := f.map_vadd 0 (Pi.single i x)
784     have s₃ := g.map_vadd 0 (Pi.single i x)
785     rw [vadd_eq_add, add_zero] at s₂ s₃
786     replace h₂ := h i 0
787     simp only [Pi.single_zero] at h₂
788     rwa [s₂, s₃, h₂, vadd_right_cancel_iff] at s₁
789   · exact h₂
790 
791 /-- Two affine maps from a Pi-type of modules `(i : ι) → φv i` are equal if they are equal in their
792   operation on `Pi.single` and `ι` is nonempty.  Analogous to `LinearMap.pi_ext`. See also
793   `pi_ext_zero`, which instead of `Nonempty ι` requires agreement at 0. -/
794 theorem pi_ext_nonempty [Nonempty ι] (h : ∀ i x, f (Pi.single i x) = g (Pi.single i x)) :
795     f = g := by
796   apply pi_ext_zero h
797   inhabit ι
798   rw [← Pi.single_zero default]
799   apply h
800 
801 /-- This is used as the ext lemma instead of `AffineMap.pi_ext_nonempty` for reasons explained in
802 note [partially-applied ext lemmas]. Analogous to `LinearMap.pi_ext'` -/
803 @[ext (iff := false)]
804 theorem pi_ext_nonempty' [Nonempty ι] (h : ∀ i, f.comp (LinearMap.single _ _ i).toAffineMap =
805     g.comp (LinearMap.single _ _ i).toAffineMap) : f = g := by
806   refine pi_ext_nonempty fun i x => ?_
807   convert AffineMap.congr_fun (h i) x
808 
809 end Ext
810 
811 end Pi
812 
813 end Ring

815 section CommRing
816 
817 variable [CommRing k] [AddCommGroup V1] [AffineSpace V1 P1] [AddCommGroup V2]
818 variable [Module k V1] [Module k V2]
819 
820 /-- `homothety c r` is the homothety (also known as dilation) about `c` with scale factor `r`. -/
821 def homothety (c : P1) (r : k) : P1 →ᵃ[k] P1 :=
822   r • (id k P1 -ᵥ const k P1 c) +ᵥ const k P1 c
823 
824 theorem homothety_def (c : P1) (r : k) :
825     homothety c r = r • (id k P1 -ᵥ const k P1 c) +ᵥ const k P1 c :=
826   rfl
827 
828 theorem coe_homothety (c : P1) (r : k) : homothety c r = fun p => r • (p -ᵥ c) +ᵥ c :=
829   rfl
830 
831 theorem homothety_apply (c : P1) (r : k) (p : P1) : homothety c r p = r • (p -ᵥ c : V1) +ᵥ c :=
832   rfl
833 
834 @[simp]
835 theorem homothety_linear (c : P1) (r : k) : (homothety c r).linear = r • LinearMap.id := by
836   simp [homothety]
837 
838 theorem homothety_eq_lineMap (c : P1) (r : k) (p : P1) : homothety c r p = lineMap c p r :=
839   rfl
840 
841 @[simp]
842 theorem homothety_one (c : P1) : homothety c (1 : k) = id k P1 := by
843   ext p
844   simp [homothety_apply]
845 
846 @[simp]
847 theorem homothety_apply_same (c : P1) (r : k) : homothety c r c = c :=
848   lineMap_same_apply c r
849 
850 theorem homothety_mul_apply (c : P1) (r₁ r₂ : k) (p : P1) :
851     homothety c (r₁ * r₂) p = homothety c r₁ (homothety c r₂ p) := by
852   simp only [homothety_apply, mul_smul, vadd_vsub]
853 
854 theorem homothety_mul (c : P1) (r₁ r₂ : k) :
855     homothety c (r₁ * r₂) = (homothety c r₁).comp (homothety c r₂) :=
856   ext <| homothety_mul_apply c r₁ r₂
857 
858 @[simp]
859 theorem homothety_zero (c : P1) : homothety c (0 : k) = const k P1 c := by
860   ext p
861   simp [homothety_apply]
862 
863 @[simp]
864 theorem homothety_add (c : P1) (r₁ r₂ : k) :
865     homothety c (r₁ + r₂) = r₁ • (id k P1 -ᵥ const k P1 c) +ᵥ homothety c r₂ := by
866   simp only [homothety_def, add_smul, vadd_vadd]
867 
868 theorem homothety_eq_iff_of_mul_eq_one {c p q : P1} {r₁ r₂ : k} (h : r₁ * r₂ = 1) :
869     homothety c r₁ p = q ↔ homothety c r₂ q = p := by
870   obtain h' : r₂ * r₁ = 1 := mul_eq_one_comm.mp h
871   refine ⟨fun h1 ↦ ?_, fun h1 ↦ ?_⟩
872   all_goals
873     rw [← h1, ← homothety_mul_apply]
874     simp [h, h']
875 
876 theorem homothety_injective [Module.IsTorsionFree k V1] [IsCancelMulZero k] (c : P1) {r : k}
877     (hr : r ≠ 0) :
878     Function.Injective (homothety c r) :=
879   fun _ _ h ↦ by simpa [homothety_def, hr] using h
880 
881 @[simp]
882 theorem homothety_inj [Module.IsTorsionFree k V1] [IsCancelMulZero k] (c : P1) {r : k} (hr : r ≠ 0)
883     {p q : P1} :
884     homothety c r p = homothety c r q ↔ p = q :=
885   (homothety_injective c hr).eq_iff
886 
887 /-- `homothety` as a multiplicative monoid homomorphism. -/
888 def homothetyHom (c : P1) : k →* P1 →ᵃ[k] P1 where
889   toFun := homothety c
890   map_one' := homothety_one c
891   map_mul' := homothety_mul c
892 
893 @[simp]
894 theorem coe_homothetyHom (c : P1) : ⇑(homothetyHom c : k →* _) = homothety c :=
895   rfl
896 
897 /-- `homothety` as an affine map. -/
898 def homothetyAffine (c : P1) : k →ᵃ[k] P1 →ᵃ[k] P1 :=
899   ⟨homothety c, (LinearMap.lsmul k _).flip (id k P1 -ᵥ const k P1 c),
900     Function.swap (homothety_add c)⟩
901 
902 @[simp]
903 theorem coe_homothetyAffine (c : P1) : ⇑(homothetyAffine c : k →ᵃ[k] _) = homothety c :=
904   rfl
905

914 /-- Applying an affine map to an affine combination of two points yields an affine combination of
915 the images. -/
916 theorem Convex.combo_affine_apply {x y : E} {a b : 𝕜} {f : E →ᵃ[𝕜] F} (h : a + b = 1) :
917     f (a • x + b • y) = a • f x + b • f y := by
918   simp only [Convex.combo_eq_smul_sub_add h, ← vsub_eq_sub]
919   exact f.apply_lineMap _ _ _
